title: Excessive hydration for mostly static pages
summary: Framework pages hydrate large component trees even when most content is static.
rationale: Hydration shifts work to the client and can waste CPU on low-interactivity pages.

impact.notes: Impact increases on high-traffic routes, large datasets, frequently rendered pages, or repeated background work.

remediation.guidance: Use islands/partial hydration, server components, static rendering, or progressive enhancement.
remediation.tradeoffs: Framework conventions, readability, caching correctness, and deployment topology should be considered before changing behavior.
